**0. Headline**

- Put/call volume ratio on the headline kept set is **0.74** → tag **CALL** (2,381,388 call contracts vs 1,770,314 put contracts across 70 strikes) —
- **on the 8 Pass-B mega-caps (IWM, GLD, TLT, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN)**. That is this file's entire population:
- the relative screen in §6 ran over the same 8 names on this date, and its universe widened to the top ~60 US names by cash volume on 2026-11-05, when it became the routine's headline metric.

- **That headline is not the whole story, and one caveat changes how it should be read.** 57.1% of the kept volume sits in contracts whose theoretical value is below $0.05 —
- real contracts, trivial premium dollars. Strip those out and the ratio **1.44 → PUT**: the economically meaningful flow today was put-heavy, not call-heavy.
- Both readings are published below; the tag follows the headline set, and the economic slice is the one to act on.

- Weighting each contract by its theoretical value settles it: **$1,995,247** of premium changed hands in the kept set, and the put side took **$1,549,219** against **$446,027** of calls —
- a dollar-weighted put/call of **3.47**. The reads are: contract count CALL, premium dollars PUT.

Two further distortions sit on top of both numbers:

- **59 of 70** kept rows expire today (91.8% of kept volume). 0DTE flow is retail/event-driven and washes out within hours; the non-0DTE remnant is almost pure call buying.
- **7 kept rows** sit on open interest under 50 (277,226 contracts).
- Contracts opened during the session carry OI of 1–30, so their V/OI ratio is 100–70,000× and they take the top of any naive ranking with no meaning attached.

**6. Relative-volume screen — introduced on this date; the routine's headline metric from 2026-11-05**

- **Where this section sits, and why.** The routine's spec says the relative screen is the headline metric, and from **2026-11-05** onward that is exactly what the artifacts do —
- the relative screen leads, the absolute book is the secondary continuity section.
- **This file is the transition day**: the screen was *introduced* here, over the legacy 8-name Pass-B universe, because the wider universe and the engine landed together on 11-05.
- So on this date it is published as a supplementary section rather than the headline — that is a fact about the date, not a competing claim about the metric.
- (An earlier version of this title read "supplementary — not the headline metric", which read as a contradiction of the spec; corrected 2026-11-06.)

- **Why the universe had to widen.** A relative screen over a fixed universe can only find anomalies *inside* that universe, and the 8 Pass-B names are all mega-caps:
- a relative screen over them cannot surface a mid-cap, **because there are none in it**.
- That is the reason the screen's universe became the top ~60 US names by cash volume on 2026-11-05 —
- and the reason a reader must know which population a number describes. **The relative screen in this section covers the same 8 Pass-B mega-caps as §0, §3, §4 and §5**;
- the absolute V/OI ranking structurally hands the top of the book to the largest chains.

- This screen normalises each contract against its own context:
- **peer ratio** (median volume of the other strikes with vol ≥ 50 in the same underlying + expiry + side), **share of expiry-side**, **share of the whole chain**, **options volume ÷ cash volume**, and **own-history** (the name's total options volume today ÷ its own 10-session average from Cboe's historical service).
- Composite = z(peer) + z(expiry share) + z(opt % cash) + z(V/OI) + 1.5·z(own-history). Every component is published so the ranking can be re-weighted.

**Cross-tape agreement**

- **Open interest: 80/80 exact** between the Cboe and Yahoo tapes across the 80 top-10 contracts. The V/OI denominator is independently corroborated.
- **ITM/OTM: 80/80 agree** with Yahoo's own `inTheMoney` field, confirming the side-aware labelling rule.
- **Underlying close: 8/8 exact** across Cboe, Yahoo daily bars and Nasdaq `secondaryData`.
- **IV is only interpretable on the non-0DTE rows.** On the 12 economically real rows with DTE > 0 the Cboe-vs-Yahoo gap is a **median 4.2 vol points** (max 8.9) —
- a normal rate/dividend assumption difference.
- On same-day rows the gap explodes (median 66 vol points on penny prints, max 206) because after the close a 0DTE option has essentially no time value left, so the IV is an artifact of the closing print (e.g.
- NVDA 210C: Cboe 243.6% vs Yahoo 37.5%, `theo` $0.0000, `delta` 0.0000, last trade $0.01 after a -99.3% session).
- **The IV column in §1 is Cboe's (the chain of record) and should not be read on 0DTE rows**; every affected row is flagged in place.
